problem: Earlier embodied-AI surveys were written before the multimodal large model (MLM) era, which the authors date to about 2023. The two post-2023 surveys each cover a narrow slice: vision-language-action models, or embodied AI for smart manufacturing. No survey jointly covers MLMs, world models (WMs), embodied agents, recent robot hardware and simulators across perception, interaction, agents and sim-to-real.
motivation: MLMs and world models now provide strong perception, reasoning and physical-law comprehension, so embodied agents are seen as the natural carriers of MLMs and a route to AGI. Current MLM-based agents still lack long-term memory, understanding of complex intentions, and task decomposition. The field is growing quickly and has no organized map aligning 'cyber space' (disembodied AI) with the 'physical world' (embodied AI).
key_idea: Organize embodied AI around an 'ABC' agent model (AI brain as an embodied world model, Body, Cross-modal sensors), with a taxonomy covering robots, simulators, embodied perception (active visual perception + VLN), embodied interaction (EQA + grasping), embodied agents (task/action planning), and sim-to-real adaptation (world models, data, transfer paradigms); the paper also introduces the ARIO unified robot-data standard and dataset.
insight: The survey's main navigation-relevant framing splits VLN methods into two families. Memory-Understanding based methods model history via graphs, semantic maps, history encoders or LLMs (e.g., HOP, NaviLLM, NaVid) and remain mainstream because VLN is a POMDP. Future-Prediction based methods include waypoint predictors (BGBL/ETPNav), lookahead/NeRF-style future-feature prediction (HNR), model-based RL (LookBY) and LLM 'imagination' (MiC); the authors expect this family to grow with world models, especially in continuous environments. For embodied agents, they argue the bottleneck lies in low-level action planning rather than high-level task planning: RoboGPT reaches 96% task-planning accuracy but only 60% overall task completion. They also argue that an action planner without an embodied world model cannot simulate physical laws.
method: ABC framework: the embodied agent is decomposed into an AI brain (MLM + embodied world model), a Body (robot embodiment executing actions and using tools) and Cross-modal sensors (active multimodal perception).

Robots & simulators review: six robot morphologies (fixed-base, wheeled, tracked, quadruped, humanoid, biomimetic); 11 general simulators compared on physics/rendering/ROS/parallelism features (Genesis, Isaac Sim/Gym, Gazebo, PyBullet, MuJoCo, etc.); real-scene simulators (SAPIEN, VirtualHome, AI2-THOR, iGibson, TDW, Matterport3D/Habitat, InfiniteWorld) and automated scene generation (RoboGen, Holodeck, PhyScene, ProcTHOR).

Embodied perception: active visual perception (traditional/semantic vSLAM, projection/voxel/point-based 3D scene understanding, active exploration). VLN dataset table (R2R, R4R, VLN-CE, Touchdown, REVERIE, SOON, DDN, ALFRED, OVMM, BEHAVIOR-1K, CVDN, DialFRED). VLN methods split into Memory-Understanding vs Future-Prediction families.

Embodied interaction: EQA dataset table (EQA v1, MT-EQA, MP3D-EQA, IQUAD, VideoNavQA, SQA3D, K-EQA, OpenEQA, HM-EQA, S-EQA, EXPRESS-Bench); neural-network vs LLM/VLM EQA methods (frontier-based exploration, conformal-prediction stopping); language-guided grasping datasets and end-to-end (CLIPort, CROG, Reasoning Grasping, SemGrasp) vs modular (F3RM, GaussianGrasper) approaches.

Embodied agents: high-level task planning via LLM emergent abilities (code or natural language, Socratic multi-turn), via visual feedback from detectors / 3D scene graphs (SayPlan, ConceptGraphs), or via VLMs (EmbodiedGPT, LEO, PaLM-E, RT series). Low-level action planning via API/policy libraries (hierarchical) vs end-to-end VLA models.

Sim-to-real: embodied world models categorized as generation-based (Sora, 3D-VLA), prediction-based latent (JEPA family, iVideoGPT) and knowledge-driven (real2sim2real, Holodeck, GRUtopia). Real vs simulated data collection. Five transfer paradigms: Real2Sim2Real, TRANSIC, domain randomization, system identification, Lang4Sim2Real.

ARIO (All Robots In One): a unified data standard for multi-morphology robot control/motion data with precise timestamps and multiple sensory modalities, plus a dataset of approximately 3 million episodes from 258 series and 321,064 tasks.

setting.training_data: n/a (survey); proposes the ARIO dataset (~3M episodes, 258 series, 321,064 tasks) but trains no model in this paper
setting.simulator: n/a (reviews Isaac Sim, Habitat/Matterport3D, AI2-THOR, iGibson, etc.)

numbers_note: Survey paper with no experimental results of its own. Tables only list dataset statistics (e.g., R2R size 21,567; REVERIE 21,702; SOON 3,848; MP3D-EQA 1,136; HM-EQA 500) and qualitative method/simulator comparisons; there are no benchmark metric tables.
results: No quantitative results. The contributions are a taxonomy of embodied AI in the MLM/WM era, comparison tables of simulators and of VLN, EQA and grasping datasets, and the ARIO dataset standard with ~3M episodes (258 series, 321,064 tasks). It closes with five future directions: high-quality robot datasets, long-horizon task execution, causal reasoning, a unified evaluation benchmark, and security/privacy.
limitations: Navigation coverage is thin: VLN gets one short subsection with a small method table. ObjectNav, ImageNav, PointNav and other goal-driven navigation tasks are not covered, and there are no quantitative cross-method comparisons.

Some categorizations and descriptions are loose. FILM (ALFRED instruction following) and LM-Nav are grouped with VLN graph/memory methods, and the Matterport3D description slides into Habitat. The ARIO dataset is only briefly described, with no experiments validating its utility.
builds_on: Embodied AI for smart manufacturing / ABC model (Ren et al. 2024)
